Blind shaping — isolated-session download destination. No tools used, no candidate inspected, nothing executed. All statements below are design-time claims, not results.

## R table (native form)

| R | Obligation (what must hold) | Oracle | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Isolated download completes; correct bytes land in the requested destination; default and other isolated sessions keep their own config/destinations | Actual later downloads in each session; directory readback only as proxy | settled |
| R1 | Invalid request, failed connect/setup/post-processing → no new isolation intent, no durable binding; flagless later requests and fresh-daemon state unchanged | Binding file diff + next-request behavior + restart | settled |
| R2 | Whole-request success on a compatible isolated connection persists intent across omission, false (≠ close), repetition, reconnect, daemon restart | Repeat/reconnect/restart matrix | settled |
| R3 | Committed intent + existing BrowserContext/target/URL/storage survive ordinary later errors and compatible reuse; dead browser may need new context/restore; a failed request's new context must never publish success | Error-then-download; kill-browser-then-reconnect | settled |
| R4 | Explicit close clears intent/binding and disposes own context under available transport; legacy/pinned formats, user env, owned-vs-external, main recording-current-page stay compatible | Close vs false; legacy binding load; main-context run | settled |
| R5 | Launch and action envelopes separate; later action failure does not undo a completed launch; mandatory in-request work may still invalidate before success | Launch-then-failing-action; in-request mandatory-step failure | settled |
| R6 | Cooperative partition only; best-effort cleanup when transport/host gone; still no false publication, no corruption of other contexts; residuals/retries measured | Transport-unavailable teardown; residual count | settled scope |
| R7 | Local fix only; no public flags/wire formats/unrelated features/remote publication | Diff surface | settled |

Flagged unknowns (all shapes): (U1) whether Browser.setDownloadBehavior addressed with a page sessionId (browser.rs:2350-2362) scopes to that page's context or to the browser default; (U2) whether browserContextId is accepted by the target Chrome build alongside/instead of a session; (U3) CDP has no download-behavior readback, so directory inspection is a proxy only; (U4) allowAndName yields GUID filenames — "correct bytes in requested destination" may need a rename keyed off downloadWillBegin; (U5) Target.createBrowserContext disposeOnDetach default false is assumed relied on for R2 reconnect survival, unverified in this codebase.

---

## Shape A — scoped call-site + commit-on-success

Parts. A1 destination resolver (canonicalize, validate/create) run before any CDP call. A2 set_download_behavior gains scope: when primary_browser_context_id is Some (browser.rs:1469-1479), send at browser level with browserContextId, no page session; otherwise unchanged. A3 DaemonState.download_intent, written only after CDP Ok and after mandatory in-request work. A4 reapply hook on attach/context-recreate, alongside apply_tab_binding_on_attach (actions.rs:3179-3263) and the context_recreated branch (3200-3212, browser.rs:727). A5 destination persisted as a sibling field of browser_context_id in the binding (3140-3168), reusing the persist-failure warning (3049-3064). A6 clear in handle_close beside the existing dispose/clear block (5499-5510).

Forward effects. Observed (from supplied source): the isolate path already threads a context id through save/load/dispose (3153, 3265-3269, browser.rs:706-738, 1505-1525), so a sibling field rides existing commit, warning and rollback machinery. Inferred: the base call sends no browserContextId and does pass a page session, so cross-session destination bleed is consistent with default-scope resolution. Guessed: scope alone leaves GUID filenames; a rename/mapping step is likely required for R0.

Harmful branches. Binding-schema change breaks legacy readers (R4). Reapply resurrects a destination in a recreated context the user never re-requested. Hard error when Chrome rejects browserContextId would break sessions that never download.

Weakest falsifiable predictions. (a) With browserContextId, a concurrent default-context session's destination is untouched — falsified if U1/U2 resolve badly. (b) Intent survives restart — falsified if reapply lands only in connect_external_cdp (3271-3290) and misses auto_launch (3935-4012) or handle_launch cdp-port/auto-connect branches (4952-5006). (c) No rename layer needed (U4).

Negative discriminators. Configure ours, then download in a third-party session and in default: destinations must be unchanged. Unwritable destination: assert no binding write, no download_intent, unchanged flagless behavior before and after restart. Error-then-download: intent persists. Kill browser, reconnect with context_recreated=true: must reapply or refuse, never report success on the new context.

Rejected alternatives. Configure only at launch (fails R2 reconnect/recreate). Page.setDownloadBehavior (page-scoped, dies with target, deprecated). Env-var destination (R7 public surface).

Compatibility cost. Low-moderate: one binding field, one extra CDP roundtrip per attach, one new error class.

---

## Shape B — declarative session download policy reconciler

Parts. B1 SessionDownloadPolicy { path, scope, generation } in DaemonState. B2 idempotent reconcile_download_policy(state) invoked at end of every launch/attach/context-recreate. B3 staged proposal promoted to state+binding only on whole-request success, mirroring last_persisted_binding (3155-3167). B4 teardown wired into handle_close and unregister_owned_context (browser.rs:1493-1499). B5 residual/retry counters surfaced through the existing warning channel (3049-3064) when transport is gone.

Forward effects. Observed: the reconcile-on-attach idiom already exists (apply_tab_binding_on_attach), so a second reconciler is idiomatic and reuses rollback (4650-4660). Inferred: idempotence makes omission/repetition/false trivially satisfied — the flagless request re-runs a no-op. Guessed: ordering against install_network_controls_or_close (3966, 4961, 2397-2409) matters; download config applied before Fetch interception may interact with intercepted responses.

Harmful branches. Reconciler firing on unrelated commands can re-publish intent a failed request created (direct R1/R3 hazard) unless generation gating is exact. Attach-time reconcile can resurrect intent after a close whose binding clear failed. More CDP chatter on hot paths.

Weakest falsifiable predictions. (a) "Reconcile is a no-op when nothing changed" — falsified by unstable canonicalization (symlink, trailing slash) causing churn. (b) Policy never touches default scope for isolated sessions — falsified if the reconciler also runs on the main/default path used by recording-current-page (R4).

Negative discriminators. Close, then flagless request: assert no download config applied anywhere. Force binding-clear failure, then reconnect: intent must not return. Trigger network-control install failure after policy staging: nothing may have been published.

Rejected alternatives. Timer-driven reconcile like autosave (unmeasurable, R6). Reconcile inside handle_close only (fails R2/R3 recovery).

Compatibility cost. High: broadest touch surface, greatest R4 regression risk.

---

## Shape C — transport-free capture (no setDownloadBehavior)

Parts. Extend the existing per-session Fetch handler (3962, 4956) to detect content-disposition and stream bytes to the destination itself.

Forward effects. Observed: the fetch handler is already installed per session. Inferred: strongest R1/R6 story — no browser-global state is mutated at all. Guessed: blob:, data:, PDF-viewer and renderer-initiated downloads are not capturable, so R0 correct-bytes fails for common cases; proxy-auth path (4941-4950) is perturbed.

Harmful branches. Memory blowup on large files; changed network semantics for every session sharing the handler; silently different download set than the browser's own.

Weakest prediction. "All download types yield correct bytes." Very weak.

Negative discriminators. Blob/data-URL download; 2 GB file; download during proxy auth.

Rejected alternatives. N/A — C is itself the fallback if U2 fails.

---

## Binary R × Shape fit-check (unknown ⇒ fail)

| R | A | B | C | Failure notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL | A/B: U1/U2/U4 unprobed (scope acceptance + GUID naming). C: non-network download classes uncovered. |
| R1 | PASS | FAIL | PASS | B: reconciler can re-publish a failed request's staged policy unless generation gating is proven exact. |
| R2 | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL | A: reapply coverage across three launch branches unproven; U5 (disposeOnDetach) unprobed. B: same U5 + no-op stability unproven. C: no durable browser state, restart intent unproven. |
| R3 | FAIL | FAIL | PASS | A/B: context_recreated recovery path (browser.rs:727, actions:3200-3212) must refuse-or-reapply without publishing; unprobed. |
| R4 | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL | A: binding schema addition vs legacy readers unproven. B: reconciler also traverses main/default path (recording-current-page). C: alters owned-vs-external semantics wholesale. |
| R5 | PASS | FAIL | FAIL | A3 separates commit from launch. B: reconcile at end of every request blurs envelopes. C: capture failure mid-action ambiguous. |
| R6 | FAIL | PASS | PASS | A: no residual/retry measurement part. |
| R7 | PASS | PASS | FAIL | C touches unrelated network features. |

---

## Conditional survivor

A, conditional on U2 and U4, plus one borrowed part: import B5 (residual/retry counters on the existing warning channel) to close A's R6 gap, and import B3's staged-proposal discipline verbatim into A3. If U2 fails (context-scoped behavior unsupported by the target build), the survivor becomes A-with-refusal: isolated sessions must refuse download configuration rather than fall back to default scope; C stays a last resort and would fail R7 as scoped.

Blocking probes, in order. (1) U2: does Browser.setDownloadBehavior accept browserContextId on real Chrome, browser-level, and does the default context stay unmodified — oracle is a later actual download in a default session, not directory readback. (2) U4: does allowAndName require a rename step to satisfy "correct bytes in requested destination". (3) U5: does the isolated context survive daemon detach/reconnect (disposeOnDetach default). (4) Reapply coverage across auto_launch, handle_launch cdp-url/cdp-port/auto-connect. (5) Failed-request non-publication end-to-end, including restart. (6) Transport-unavailable teardown residual count. Until (1)-(3) return, every R0/R2 cell above stays FAIL by rule.
